blockers.what: The one-time eventsUnreadable warning is lost when the start fails after the events file is opened. EventLog's constructor removes the unreadable lines from the file at once (events.ts:56), but the warning is appended only after the bind (http.ts:388-390). A start that fails in between (a busy port, a setup that throws) leaves a cleaned file and no warning, and the next successful start finds 0 unreadable lines, so the person is never told lines were removed. Reproduced: torn events file, start on a held port -> EADDRINUSE, file after it is "", next start's events are only ['service.started']. (apps/agent/src/service/events.ts:54-56 with apps/agent/src/service/http.ts:179-184, 354-365, 388-390, found by the `unit` tier)

close() can resolve while a 'stopping' refusal's onRefused hook is still running. The refused request is outside drain.work, so the drain does not wait for it; when the last in-flight request ends, finish() closes all connections and releases the lock, close() resolves, the client gets ECONNRESET instead of the 503, and the hook (the door's journal write) completes after close() returned. Reproduced: hook gated, in-flight /slow released, close() resolved with the hook unfinished, the refused call ended 'error ECONNRESET', the hook finished afterwards. Same shape as the guard's refusals, but at stopping it is the expected timing, not a corner. (apps/agent/src/service/http.ts:316-327 (refusal outside drain.work), 368-380 (finish), 433-438 (close), found by the `unit` tier)

Doc comments still describe the unreadable-lines count as a degraded state, which this node removed: EventLog.unreadable says 'the service reports the count as degraded for this run only' and the constructor comment says 'a degraded status does not outlive what caused it'; messages.ts calls the catalogue's sentences 'the degraded reason beside the service's status'. events.ts is one of this node's edit targets. (apps/agent/src/service/events.ts:41-46, 54-55; apps/agent/src/service/messages.ts:5-6, found by the `unit` tier)

After the bind, the HTTP server has no 'error' listener: the one used for listen is removed (http.ts:358). A later server-level error (Node's net server emits 'error' on an accept failure such as EMFILE) would be an unhandled 'error' event and end the daemon. Inherited from N-005, read from code and Node's net semantics, not reproduced. (apps/agent/src/service/http.ts:354-361, found by the `unit` tier)

RouteContext carries no stopping signal. A long /mcp stream learns of a stop only when the drain deadline (8 s) passes and finish() calls closeAllConnections(), with no journal entry for the cut call. N-008 Test 17 requires the door to close the stream itself before the deadline and journal it. (N-008 (plan line 326: Modify apps/agent/src/service/http.ts, RouteContext gains an AbortSignal); shell side apps/agent/src/service/http.ts:48-58, 398-402, found by the `seam` tier)

Three shell gaps the daemon will hit: (1) after the bind the server has no 'error' listener (http.ts:358 removes it), so an accept error such as EMFILE is an uncaught exception; (2) EventLog removes unreadable lines in its constructor (events.ts:56) before the warning is appended (http.ts:388-390), so a start that fails in setup or bind loses the warning for good; (3) close() waits only on drain.work, not on onRefused calls already started for guard or 'stopping' refusals, so the door's journal write can race the lock release. The events.ts doc comment (lines 44, 54-55) still says the count is reported as degraded. (N-011 (plan line 424, Test 26) which edits apps/agent/src/service/http.ts and events.ts, found by the `seam` tier)

N-006 plans DoorRejection as a hand-copied literal union of the shell's onRefused values. Nothing ties it to the exported RefusalReason, so a reason the shell adds later reaches Journal.record as an untyped code with no compile error. (N-006 apps/agent/src/journal/journal.ts (plan line 279), found by the `seam` tier)

interaction: onRefused fires for every refused request on every path, not only the door's. Once the door journals the hook (N-006 DoorRejection includes 'stopping'), each stop's 8 s drain can put rows into the agents' journal and SCR-24 'Последние отказы' that no agent caused: Fabric's host polling /fabric/v1/events, the page's own /api requests. The refusal list then counts refusals that are not agents' and shows rows with no agent for the refusalLine '$AGENT$: ...' format (apps/agent/src/service/http.ts:126-131, 316-328; plan N-006 DoorRejection, N-015 test 7, N-014 test 3 (rejection_door), found by the `product` tier)

an agent that calls during a stop receives a bare HTTP 503 whose body is a Russian sentence by default, not the contract envelope of spec section 2.3; the agent and its person would read 'Okolos Agent останавливается...' rather than a retryable refusal (apps/agent/src/service/http.ts:322-327; spec section 2.3, found by the `product` tier)

eventsUnreadable tells the person 'остальные события сохранены' / 'the other events are kept', but the same start then runs the retention trim, which drops events older than 7 days beyond the newest 1000. On a long-lived file the sentence and the file can disagree in the same minute (apps/agent/src/service/events.ts:49-58; apps/agent/_locales/ru/messages.json eventsUnreadable, found by the `product` tier)

Not product text, but the next reader takes it as the behaviour (apps/agent/src/service/events.ts:44, 54-55; apps/agent/src/service/messages.ts:5-6, found by the `product` tier)
